findings: Both captures list M2 and Chipper 2X BT for the US, and WisePad 3 for a non-US list. November changes WisePad 3 from 24 explicit codes in May to 37 including HK and twelve additional European codes.

The integrator uses iOS, Android or React Native Terminal SDK with BLE or Android-only USB. Stripe and its hardware partners issue periodic updates, including possible required security updates. Mobile readers automatically update on POS connection. The app must support updates, and failing to install a required update can prevent payment acceptance. A reader forces a reboot and disconnects 24 hours after its last boot.
The mapped source preserves the lifecycle but overcounts the displayed May WisePad 3 markets as 25 and overstates failure to install a required update as invariably blocking payments.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/mobile-readers, source-stripe-terminal-mobile-readers should describe the November 7, 2026 mobile SDK scope. An integrator connects to the mobile device's iOS, Android or React Native Terminal SDK by BLE or Android-only USB. Stripe and hardware partners release software and possible required security updates, the reader automatically updates when connecting to the POS, and the merchant application must support updating. Failing to install a required update can prevent the reader from accepting payments. The reader forces a reboot and disconnects from the POS app 24 hours after its last boot. See old raw line 10, old raw lines 18-22, new raw line 11 and new raw lines 18-22. The stable US rows cover M2 and Chipper 2X BT. WisePad 3 expands from 24 explicitly listed markets in May 1, 2026 to 37 in November. See old raw lines 14-16 and new raw lines 14-16. The current summary keeps SDK, connection and reboot flow, but it incorrectly counts 25 on the May list and turns the conditional update failure effect into an absolute.
